Plan_of_Care.content: Start over-the-counter antihistamine such as chlorphenamine 4 mg every 6 hours as needed or a once-daily non-sedating antihistamine
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Start OTC antihistamine (e.g., chlorphenamine 4 mg q6h prn or once-daily non-sedating)

Plan_of_Care.content: Educate patient on red-flag symptoms including increased lip or tongue swelling, stridor, dyspnoea, and spreading or hot erythema and advise to go to emergency department immediately if these occur
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Educate on red-flag symptoms: ↑ lip/tongue swelling, stridor, dyspnoea, spreading/hot erythema—> ED immediately

Plan_of_Care.content: Advise follow-up or emergency department visit if rash spreads or there are signs of infection; consider allergy work-up only if recurrent reactions
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Advise f/u or ED if rash spreads or signs infection; consider allergy work-up only if recurrent reactions

Plan_of_Care.content: Provide educational link on anaphylaxis, reassure patient, and invite re-contact if concerned
